data.exact_reserve_text: The 2017 underwriting loss was also signficantly impacted by a change to the Ogden discount rate. On February 27, 2017 the UK Ministry of Justice announced that the discount rate in the Ogden tables will decrease from 2.5% to minus 0.75%. As a result of this reduction the reserves held on the 2014 and prior years of account relating to UK Motor Treaty business have been adversely impacted, resulting in a GBP 52.4m strengthening to the prior year losses. The adverse impacts to the underwriting result were partially offset by a release from prior year reserves of GBP 59.2m (2016, GBP 57.6m release). This release is a result of more favourable claims development than originally anticipated and the work of our claims department in dealing with claims in an expeditious manner.

data.data_quality_notes: The `prior_year_development_gbp_m` reflects the explicitly stated gross strengthening due to the Ogden rate change. The report also mentions a net release of GBP 59.2m due to favourable claims development, but a gross figure for this component is not provided. The gross claims development triangle, when calculated, shows a total gross strengthening of GBP 171.619m for prior years (excluding 2016 and 2017), which is significantly higher than the Ogden impact alone and contradicts the narrative of a net release. Due to the explicit instruction to use gross figures and the potential for RITC distortions (Syndicate 1400 RITC accepted in 2016, tables restated) making the triangle less reliable for direct PYD calculation, the explicit gross Ogden impact is used as the primary figure for prior year development.
